requirements.requirement: AIDE (or equivalent integrity tool) installed on node1
requirements.summary: dnf install -y aide completed successfully (aide-0.19.2-5.el9_8.1.x86_64 installed).

requirements.requirement: AIDE configured to scope monitoring to /etc with a meaningful attribute set
requirements.summary: /etc/aide.conf rewritten (original backed up) with database_in/database_out, and rule 'All=p+i+n+u+g+s+m+c+acl+selinux+xattrs+sha256' applied to '/etc All'. Config validated with aide --config-check and successfully used for init/check.
aide --init created /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz with 1187 entries; promoted to active db; sha256 hash captured. A fresh aide --check against this baseline reported 'NO differences'.

requirements.requirement: Baseline can detect later changes to /etc (core purpose of the task)
requirements.summary: A smoke-test file (/etc/aide-integrity-smoketest.conf) was created and aide --check correctly flagged it as a new entry ('f+++++++++++++++++'), directly demonstrating the change-detection mechanism works. The file was then removed and the db hash confirmed unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Baseline left in a stable, usable state reflecting current /etc (not stale or contaminated by test artifacts or unrelated boot churn)
requirements.summary: After the mandated restart, AIDE correctly flagged expected boot-time ctime churn (8 changed entries, 0 added/removed) proving the mechanism persisted and works across a real reboot. The baseline was then re-initialized against the stable post-boot state, and a final aide --check reported 'NO differences'. The smoketest file was confirmed not to persist.

requirements.requirement: Mandatory provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (513c865e...) and healthy AIDE state captured; reboot scheduled and acknowledged via systemd-run; connection dropped/timed out during reboot; post-restart boot_id (00b4c886...) confirmed different from pre-restart, matching the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart AIDE db/config persisted and detection worked, and cluster/service state (no failed units, listening sockets equivalent) was recovered.

overall_summary: The executor fully satisfied the task: AIDE was installed, configured to monitor /etc with a strong attribute set, and initialized into a baseline database. Change detection was directly demonstrated via a smoke test (new file flagged, then cleaned up). The mandatory restart protocol was completed with clear pre/post boot_id evidence, and post-restart the mechanism was shown to survive reboot and correctly flag real boot-time metadata churn, after which the baseline was re-initialized against the stable post-boot state with a final clean check. Lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot identity change and show no failed services, unsafe exposure, or package damage after the task.
limitations: Evaluation relies entirely on captured command stdout/return codes; no independent live inspection of node1 was possible.
The five /tmp/aide-check-*.log files remain on disk post-task; while low-risk and task-relevant, their retention was not explicitly verified as intentional versus incidental oversight.

AIDE's periodic-check timer/cron scheduling was probed (systemctl list-unit-files | grep aide) but the specific output was not captured in the reviewed evidence, so ongoing automated periodic checking beyond the manual baseline is indeterminate -- though the task only required establishing a baseline, not scheduling recurring checks.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace: dnf install (prerequisite), aide.conf rewrite with backup (prerequisite, original preserved as aide.conf.orig.bak), first aide.conf write used invalid 'database=' key causing a failed --init (cmd-58e3c9fbb73444e9, rc=17) which was a legitimate troubleshooting/diagnosis step corrected in the very next config rewrite (cmd-7a146fe5755b4b23) using proper 'database_in='/'database_out=' syntax -- not an unnecessary mutation, just a corrective iteration. The smoke-test file /etc/aide-integrity-smoketest.conf was created and fully removed within the same command, directly serving the material requirement of proving detection works -- bounded and reverted. Five /tmp/aide-check-*.log files were left behind (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff); these are low-risk, expected verification artifacts tied directly to the task, not unbounded residue. The reboot was a mandated action, fully recovered (no failed services, no unexpected socket exposure -- only PID changes from the restart itself). No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were identified; package/service state is clean post-task.
